reading.body:
QTS Ashburn-Moran is a 3-acre facility in Sterling with 4 MW of critical power capacity. The operator publishes no IT load or rack count; at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 4 MW of critical power would support roughly 100 racks, but this figure depends entirely on the actual workload mix and PUE efficiency, which are not published. The facility offers N, N+1, and 2N+1 redundancy options with 48-hour fuel autonomy, qualifying it for workloads requiring continuous operation with planned maintenance windows.

This Ashburn-Moran site is one of at least eight discrete QTS buildings across Loudoun and Prince William counties and Sterling, Virginia. Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities, but only 23 publish power capacity figures; Ashburn-Moran does not rank in the published top 23 for the state, placing it outside the ranked cohort by operator disclosure.

The facility is part of QTS's legacy Northern Virginia portfolio, a region the operator has held since its 2003 founding. QTS was acquired by Blackstone Infrastructure Partners in August 2021 for approximately $10 billion, but no published information indicates whether this specific site has been redeployed, upgraded, or retired since that acquisition. Whether this campus matters to AI scaling depends on factors not in the public record: current tenant mix, actual IT load deployed, connection to the local grid, and operational status under Blackstone ownership.
